issue_context.title: [Bug]:  toHaveText() fails with irrelevant error if applied to non-existing/non-visible elements
issue_context.body:
### Version

1.41.2

### Steps to reproduce

Create assertion expecting non-existing field to to have text. Ex:

```ts
test('field should be empty', async ({ page }) => {
            //case1
            await expect(page.locator('.i-do-not-exist'), 'field should be empty').toHaveText('');
            //case2
            await expect(page.locator('i-do-not-exist') , 'field should have 'abc' text').toHaveText('abc');
});     
```

### Expected behavior

the assertion should fail but signal the element do not exist instead of saying that element has '' text

### Actual behavior

case1: 

```
Locator: locator('.non-exising-element')
Expected string: ""
Received string: serializes to the same string
```

case2:

```
Error: field should have 'abc' text

    Timed out 15000ms waiting for expect(locator).toHaveText(expected)

    Locator: locator('.non-exising-element')
    Expected string: "abc"
    Received string: ""
```



### Additional context

_No response_

### Environment

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 14.3
    CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M1 Pro
    Memory: 109.13 MB / 16.00 GB
  Binaries:
    Node: 18.18.2 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v18.18.2/bin/node
  Languages:
    Bash: 3.2.57 - /bin/bash
  npmPackages:
    @playwright/test: ^1.41.2 => 1.41.2
```

review_comments: This test is not checking `.not.toHaveText()` that has changed extensively in the code. I'd recommend trimming this list to just a few, but add `.not` and any other interesting variants.
Would you keep: one boolean matcher and one text matcher for each branch?
Yeah, we should cover every branch, those are easy to mess up.
It seems like you can move `notFound` case outside of both branches.
This comment suggests that `missingReceived` is doing the exact same thing, isn't it?
Now that we only have 6 cases, maybe inlining them with exact expected error message would be easier to understand?
Not a huge fan, since it would make the test much larger. This underlines our motivation that the `waiting for locator` and `Received` value should be displayed in all the scenarios.
